desc: A'Urughs are military administered familiar units and flocks left behind by the Mongolian armies.
entities.name: A'Urughs

desc: The Ç̌äwa adapt a line formation, marching side by side and firing in order. When the first line in combat reloads their firearms, the second takes their position to fire, just to be replaced by the next one in a continuous motion.
entities.name: Ç̌äwa Line Infantry

desc: The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.
entities.name: Janissary Line Infantry

desc: A unit of light cavalry that specializes in mobile and ranged warfare, these raiders make for a fine army and a valuable addition to our ranks.
entities.name: Akıncılar

desc: The Akritai rose to prominence as the defenders of Anatolia against the eastern threats that the empire faced. These soldiers were given grants through the Decayed Theme System to cultivate and protect, as a means to provide them with a reward and a reason to defend our homeland.
entities.name: Akritai

desc: Almogavars are a class of light infantry soldiers originating from the Crown of Aragon. These quick-moving warriors serve as frontier defenders and foot soldiers. In addition to their role in the Reconquista, they have also found employment as mercenaries in Italy, the Frankokratia, and the Levant.
entities.name: Almogavars

desc: Archers support our footmen with ranged fire, allowing them to advance towards enemy lines when attacking and also helping them better protect their position when defending.
entities.name: Archers

desc: Horsemen who are more heavily armored, usually with some form of mail or full plate, to charge headlong into enemy ranks.
entities.name: Armored Horsemen

desc: A pike-and-shot formation consisting of a core of troops armed with firearms and protected by a phalanx of armored pikemen, the Arquebusiers are a formidable unit that cannot be easily countered.
entities.name: Arquebusiers

desc: Recruited from our Carpathian and Balkan lands, these light troops are well equipped to guard the peace in our border regions. Their knowledge of their homeland will make them a formidable opponent for any invader.
entities.name: Grenzer Infantry

desc: Stationed in border garrisons, these regiments of hussars will be able to patrol and secure the far reaches of our country, while keeping the strain on our treasury light.
entities.name: Grenzhussar

desc: The generalization of standing armies in the Reformation is further developing the supply needs of their soldiers, the use of a Baggage Train that follows the advance of the armies becoming commonplace.
entities.name: Baggage Train

desc: Born on the steppes and raised in the hardships between battle and iron, these riders are the bringers of doom for those who seek to oppose our rule. Their devastating charges and mastery of warfare makes them a formidable opponent.
entities.name: Banner Cavalry

desc: Regiments of seasoned hunters and foresters. These units will be unmatched in forested terrain, able to hinder and harass our enemies if they dare to enter our forests.
entities.name: Bavarian Jäger

desc: The Bedouin are a wandering people who travel through the desert regions of the Arabian Peninsula, North Africa, the Levant and Mesopotamia. Through their nomadic lifestyle, they have mastered their riding skills, and the usage of the Arabian horses makes them a formidable cavalry force.
entities.name: Bedouin Cavalry

desc: The elephant is a massive animal with far-reaching tusks and a thick hide. Its ability to traverse any kind of jungle gives the elephant a significant advantage in a very present niche of India. Additionally to this, the Bengali War Elephant has the benefit of versatility as it is capable of carrying a significant amount of supplies with it.
entities.name: Bengali Elephant Cavalry

desc: The Black Guard is an elite corps of former slaves. Raised since childhood to abide by a religious creed, they excel in archery, horsemanship, musketry, and masonry. These troops form the backbone of our army at a time when our people need protection the most.
entities.name: Black Guard

desc: The Helepolis has served many Byzantine emperors in the past. With the introduction of gunpowder and the advent of new siege machines of warfare, the city-taker artillery has now embraced its new deadly form.
entities.name: Modernized Helepolis

desc: A powerful body of heavily armored knights, the Cataphracts make up the elite of our cavalry units. Armed with a short lance named 'kontos' and covered in scale armor, these troops strike fear at the heart of our enemies. A whirlwind of steel in the form of an unstoppable wave of horsemen delivers the killing blow to all those who seek to trample our people.
entities.name: Byzantine Cataphracts

desc: The Late Medieval Cataphracts are mail-clad riders and horses alike, thundering into battle behind long lances and dense shields. Their shock charges and iron discipline are a frightening sight for our foes.
entities.name: Late Medieval Cataphracts

desc: These Reformed Cataphracts blend old Imperial drills with newer tactics, combining lances with bows and sidearms. They fight as a flexible heavy cavalry corps, able to harass at range and then finish off their foes in close combat.
entities.name: Reformed Cataphracts

desc: The Heavy Cataphracts ride in layered armor that deflects most missiles and blades. Organized into wedges of elite fighters, they break enemy lines with repeated charges that few formations can withstand.
entities.name: Heavy Cataphracts

desc: Chosen from the finest lancers, the Guard Cataphracts serve as the mounted guard of the throne and our capital. Their presence in every battle is both a weapon and a symbol, rallying our troops and terrifying our foes.
entities.name: Guard Cataphracts

desc: The Imperial Cataphracts are the culmination of centuries of cavalry tradition: armored veterans, superbly mounted and drilled to perfection. They serve as the Emperor's personal guard, able to decide campaigns with a single, well-timed charge.
entities.name: Imperial Cataphracts

desc: Caçadores (hunters), the Portuguese version of the German ''Jägers'' or the French ''Chasseurs'', are an elite light infantry unit whose mission is the defense of the Portuguese territory.
entities.name: Caçadores

desc: A motley crew of merchants and families of the soldiery, Camp Followers provide informal services to warbands on the march.
entities.name: Camp Followers

desc: The Caroleans are the Swedish and Finnish infantry of the Swedish Empire. Recruited from the peasantry, the Caroleans go under strict training and are renowned for invoking fear in the hearts of their enemies.
entities.name: Caroleans

desc: Some of the fiercest and deadliest crossbowmen in the Western Mediterranean, the Catalan Crossbowmen competed against the Genoese Crossbowmen for supremacy in this field.
entities.name: Catalan Crossbowmen

desc: Caterans are very light raiders armed with short spears and handaxes. Other than small targes and skullcaps, they are unencumbered by armor, relying instead on their swiftness for defense.
entities.name: Caterans

desc: The golden age of knighthood may be over, but the Nobility retains a presence on the battlefield as a gallant and well-armed cavalry force.
entities.name: Cavaliers

desc: Cavalrymen are light cavalry, sometimes armed with ranged weapons, used to attack enemy lines, although they may sometimes be ready to charge into close combat.
entities.name: Cavalrymen

desc: In Ethiopia, the arsenal of the Ç̌äwa encompasses the formidable curved sword known as the ''shotel'', the versatile spear called the ''tor'', and proficiency in ranged weaponry such as bows and javelins known as ''armah''. Notably, the use of protective armor, including the renowned coat of mail, is prevalent among them, further enhancing their defensive capabilities.
entities.name: Ç̌äwa Units

desc: One of the most prominent muzzle-loaded cannons of our era is the Cetbang. Armed with a cylindrical short barrel, it delivers a devastating blow with tremendous power. Such is its popularity, that it finds use in many aspects of our conduct of warfare, from protecting our ports to being the main armament of our warships and armies.
entities.name: Cetbang

desc: The 16th century did not only see improvements in artillery maneuverability but also in the attempts at standardizing the size and weight of artillery pieces.
entities.name: Chambered Cannon

desc: Champions are elite units among tribal warriors, formed by those that stand out among the ranks of the Warriors for their bravery and martial abilities
entities.name: Champions

desc: Noble warriors adorned in decorative armor and wielding bejeweled weaponry, Chieftains are expected to lead the charge and serve as exemplars to the other fighters.
entities.name: Chieftains

desc: The key part of any clan's army are their close retainers, troops bounded by ties of loyalty and familiar relationships.
entities.name: Clan Retainer Cavalry

desc: The key part of any clan's army are their close retainers, troops bounded by ties of loyalty and familiar relationships.
entities.name: Clan Retainers

desc: Reluctant soldiers obligated to fight, massed Conscripts can overwhelm a trained army through numbers alone.
entities.name: Conscripts

desc: Crossbowmen are a type of ranged fire unit that harness the increased firepower of crossbows, a much more powerful, albeit slow-reloading, projectile weapon.
entities.name: Crossbowmen

desc: Warrior monks devoted to the expansion of Christendom, the Crusader Sergeants form the elite foot vanguard of the religious military orders, pairing the Crusader Knights on foot.
entities.name: Crusader Sergeants

desc: Warrior monks devoted to the expansion of Christendom, the Crusader Sergeants form the elite foot vanguard of the religious military orders, pairing the Crusader Knights on foot.
entities.name: Crusader Sergeants

desc: Warrior monks devoted to the expansion of Christendom, the Crusader Sergeants form the elite foot vanguard of the religious military orders, pairing the Crusader Knights on foot.
entities.name: Crusader Sergeants

desc: Keeping up with the changing times, Cuirassiers are heavy cavalry that have discarded lances in favor of pistols and sabers as their primary weapon.
entities.name: Cuirassiers

desc: A regiment of women that originate from Guinea. They strike fear into the enemy ranks, and cause devastating damage.
entities.name: Dahomey Amazons

desc: The introduction of gunpowder makes the traditional bows and javelins obsolete, but gives a new edge to the Ç̌äwa.
entities.name: Ç̌äwa Arquebusiers

desc: A more established version of the Conquistador with a better insight on what they can aspire to. These men full of ambition will make empires crumble.
entities.name: Conquistadors

desc: The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.
entities.name: Janissary Arquebusiers

desc: The Kızılbaş are members of a militant Shia order made of a coalition of different tribes of Turkic-speaking background. Their religious belief plays a major role in their duty, making them both ferocious warriors and devout members of the Ṣafawiyya order.
entities.name: Kızılbaş Skirmisher

desc: Eagle Warriors are an elite class of infantry in the Aztec army. They use a number of weapons, including atlatl javelins, spears, and daggers. They are the bravest soldiers who had taken the most prisoners in battle. Commoners, as well as nobles, may become Eagle warriors on merit.
entities.name: Eagle Warriors

desc: The arquebus is the evolution of the handgonne, making it a more reliable type of gunpowder weapon as it is easier and faster to reload, making it ideal for deploying larger gunpowder fire units.
entities.name: Early Arquebusiers

desc: The powerful martial longbow, originally deployed with great impact against armored English knights in the Welsh valleys, has been adopted into the military doctrine on either side of the border.
entities.name: Warbows

desc: Paiks are foot soldiers of India who are renowned for their offensive and defensive versatility and their skill in archery. Every man serves in the Paik System as a Paik conscript, which leads to a greater quantity of troops on the field, but comes at the cost of professionalism.
entities.name: Early Paik

desc: Paiks are foot soldiers of India who are renowned for their offensive and defensive versatility and their skill in archery.
entities.name: Early Paik Infantry

desc: A professional regiment composed of lesser chieftains, these riders are not selected through connections, but rather by merit.
entities.name: Esho Cavalry

desc: Elite marksmen equipped with the long-range Baker Rifle and trained to screen the main force in small independent pickets, Experimental Riflemen represent a modern vision of infantry combat formations.
entities.name: Experimental Riflemen

desc: The Falconet is a light cannon developed in the 15th century as an evolution of the similar falcon, being more mobile while firing smaller caliber shots.
entities.name: Falconet

desc: The Farari are the elite corps of the Malian military. Appointed from privileged and common people alike, the Farari are known for their bravery and military experience.
entities.name: Farari Cavalry

desc: The Farari are the elite corps of the Malian military. Appointed from privileged and common people alike, the Farari are known for their bravery and military experience.
entities.name: Farari Infantry

desc: A Feudal Levies is formed by peasants that are drafted in times of war as part of their duty towards their feudal lord, and have some military training. These levies are to eventually be replaced by professional armies.
entities.name: Feudal Levies

desc: The flintlock musket has replaced the matchlock arquebus as the primary infantry weapon, providing greater and more accurate firepower while being easier to use and maintain.
entities.name: Flintlock Levy

desc: The shifting landscape of diplomacy and war in the Italian [

] dictates that we should not entrust our defense and sovereignty to paid condottieri. Instead, we should erect an able body of Florentine Citizen Militia, quick to mobilize and lacking no qualities when compared to any other troops, to defend our domain from prospecting conquerors.
entities.name: Florentine Citizen Militia

desc: Artillery is devastating on the battlefield, but completely useless if the enemy does not enter its firing range. A Flying Battery has the capability of relocating itself to where it is most needed and quickly redeploy before any enemy's retaliation.
entities.name: Flying Battery

desc: The backbone of every army, footmen comprise the majority of our marching troops, eager to sustain a frontline and defend our home from prospecting invaders.
entities.name: Footmen

desc: The backbone of every army, footmen comprise the majority of our marching troops, eager to sustain a frontline and defend our home from prospecting invaders.
entities.name: Footmen Levy

desc: Fusiliers are the backbone of our armies, armed with a modern ranged rifle and a bayonet that can be attached to it and enables the possibility of massed charges into enemy ranks.
entities.name: Fusiliers

desc: Gallop Cavalry is a shock unit that charges the enemy with long cavalry sabers, protected with a certain degree of armor, which is a good balance between mobility and forcefulness.
entities.name: Gallop Cavalry

desc: Heavy infantry fitted with mail and wielding two-handed axes, the fearsome Gallowglass descend from Norse sea raiders who settled along the Atlantic coast.
entities.name: Gallowglass

desc: These mountain shooters are unmatched in traversing alpine terrain and besting our foes in the treacherous mountain passes. Their light equipment and loose organization makes them perfectly equipped for high-altitude combat.
entities.name: Gebirgsschützen

desc: The Gendarmerie are the elite cavalry of the realm, recruited from the most prestigious noble families. Clad in cuirasses and armed with the finest swords and pistols, they are a formidable force on the battlefield.
entities.name: Gendarmerie

desc: Genoese Crossbowmen are a respected military unit that was used by the Genoese during the First Crusade up until now. Equipped with Genoese crossbows and the pavise, these infantrymen serve as the protection of their home as well as mercenaries in Europe.
entities.name: Genoese Crossbowmen

desc: The Ḡilmān are an elite infantrymen corps which took on the usage of firearms instead of relying on traditional weapons. Made of slave soldiers, the Ḡilmān swear absolute loyalty towards the Shah before anyone else.
entities.name: Ḡilmān

desc: Armies and troops change, but covering your enemies with flames and setting them ablaze continues to be an effective method of combat. As such, Greek Fire keeps having its presence among our armies, and it keeps being feared by our adversaries.
entities.name: Advanced Cheirosiphōnes

desc: Not only ships can benefit from the Greek Fire, but also our land troops can be equipped with hand-held devices to spew the flaming substance onto our enemies. Fire and destruction will cleave the enemy's ranks and pave a way to our advance.
entities.name: Cheirosiphōnes

desc: Evolved from earlier units equipped with explosives, these Grenadiers serve as elite vanguards for our armies. While the grenades from which their name comes are no longer their sole focus, their superior training makes them excellent assault troops.
entities.name: Grenadiers

desc: Gurkha are troops of Nepali origins (as their name are quite interchangeable) who are infamous for their unbreakable bravery and discipline in combat.
entities.name: Gurkha

desc: The Hajduk are a light infantry unit common across the Balkans and surrounding areas. Operating as autonomous bands, these frontiersmen are often driven to the mountains by fiscal oppression, legal disputes, or a desire for military glory, specializing in the disruption of supply lines and the ambushing of tax convoys.
entities.name: Hajduk

desc: The Hakkapeliitta were the fearsome Finnish cavalry known for their gruesome effectiveness on the battlefield. The name Hakkapeliitta is a Finnish modification of the names that the soldiers of the Holy Roman Empire gave them, stemming from their battle cry 'Hakkaa päälle!', or 'Hack on them!'/'Cut them down!'. The Hakkapeliitta were feared for their sudden and savage attacks that shocked the enemy into submission.
entities.name: Hakkapeliitta

desc: Halberdiers are units of soldiers that wield polearms, such as halberds, which are used for close combat, both offensively and defensively.
entities.name: Halberdiers

desc: Auxiliary units that often accompanied their Mamlūk counterparts, these light and quick troops will offer great support to their parent forces on the battlefield.
entities.name: Ḥalqah

desc: Handgonners wield a new type of gunpowder-filled weapon that fires deadly lead shells, wreaking havoc on enemy lines, though they need to be fully protected as their handgonnes are very slow to reload.
entities.name: Handgonners

desc: (This is just a template, should never be seen)
entities.name: Heavy Cavalry

desc: A heavier type of cavalry, fully armored and trained for shock charges, thanks to its heavy armor and armament, which should lead to the disruption of the enemy line.
entities.name: Heavy Cavalrymen

desc: (This is just a template, should never be seen)
entities.name: Heavy Infantry

desc: Heavy Lancers are the heaviest type of shock cavalry possible, and feature fully armored armor and the finest shock lances. Their charges are designed to completely disrupt the enemy formation, and they are also much more protected from enemy fire at range.
entities.name: Heavy Lancers

desc: Elite light troops composed of expert hunters. Their knowledge of our own terrain will increase our ability to fight in dense forests, although their equipment is not suited for prolonged fighting.
entities.name: Hessian Jäger

desc: Mounted upon the agile Irish hobby horse, Hobelars are spearmen able to swiftly traverse rough terrain.
entities.name: Hobelars

desc: Lightly-armored fighters mounted upon swift horses, bands of Horsemen have the mobility to harass, charge, and pursue.
entities.name: Horsemen

desc: It is believed modern howitzers have their name from the Houfnice artillery developed by the Hussites in the 15th century. These short-barreled guns were mounted on wagons and used on the field of battle to fire balls and canisters in support of the infantry.
entities.name: Houfnice

desc: Drawing inspiration from the storied legacy of King Matthias I Corvinus' cavalry, this idea introduces the 'Royal Hussar Regiments,' granting a formidable edge to Hungary's light cavalry forces. With their swift and fearless charges, these regiments are a symbol of Hungarian martial prowess, proving indispensable on the battlefields of Europe.
entities.name: Hungarian Hussars

desc: Hunters are light infantry designed to attack enemy formations from long range as they approach, attempting to disorganize them and make their own firepower much less effective.
entities.name: Hunters

desc: The hussars were originally light cavalry troops originating in Central Europe that were used for scouting, but with the decline of the old feudal army they were switched over to professional regiments.
entities.name: Hussars

desc: The Hwacha deliver devastating firepower through their barrages of rocket-powered arrows or iron-headed bolts. Their maneuverability forces them to take a more defensive role in battles.
entities.name: Hwacha

desc: The robust elephants are a great animal for the transportation of goods for our armies. Although slower than horses and other pack animals, the pure strength of the elephants allows us to carry a great quantity of food and supply into enemy territory.
entities.name: Elephant Auxiliary

desc: The elephant is a massive animal with far-reaching tusks and a thick hide. Its ability to traverse any kind of jungle gives the elephant a significant advantage in a very present niche of India.
entities.name: Elephant Cavalry

desc: Skilled soldiers who wear iron helmets for protection and wield muskets as their primary firearms, these troops have come to dominate the battlefields. They serve as infantry troops in various armies across Africa, under the banner of some of the most powerful rulers. Loading their muskets with black powder and lead balls, aiming and firing at their enemies from a distance, their thunderous volleys have stopped many charges in their tracks, whilst their iron helmets provide vital head protection during battles and skirmishes. These musketeers play a crucial role in the evolution of warfare, introducing firearms as a significant force on the battlefield.
entities.name: Iron-Helmet Musketeers

desc: Powerful and heavy cavalry set to punch through the enemy's frontline and deliver a deadly blow to their morale and formation.
entities.name: Iron Pagoda Cavalry

desc: Jaguar Warriors are an elite class of infantry in the Aztec army. They fight with a mācuahuitl, a wooden club studded with obsidian blades. To become a Jaguar warrior, a man had to have captured at least four prisoners in battle.
entities.name: Jaguar Warriors

desc: The Jazāyerchi are the elite musketeers of the empire. Equipped with heavy flintlock muskets with superior firepower and accuracy and exposed to constant drilling, the Jazāyerchi manage to overcome even the most one-sided odds in battle.
entities.name: Jazāyerchi

desc: The Jonow are slaves who accompany the Kèlè-Koun and their soldiers as carriers of their military equipment.
entities.name: Jonow Auxiliary

desc: Bands of skirmishers borne of the rugged hills and peaty bogs, Kerns are light raiders armed with darts and daggers.
entities.name: Kerns

desc: The Khmer Ballista Elephants are a fearsome presence on the battlefield, utilizing a double-stringed crossbow mounted on top.
entities.name: Khmer Ballista Elephants

desc: Strong cavalry armed with a lance, these shock troops are meant to break through enemy lines and devastate our foes' forces.
entities.name: Lancers

desc: The Landsknechte combine, in a same unit, pikemen with the infamous ''Doppelsöldner'', 'double-pay men' carrying two-handed swords, while being supported by arquebusiers at their flanks.
entities.name: Landsknechte

desc: Inspired by the Genitour Moorish cavalry, the Lanzas de Castilla are mobile cavalry that, however, charges into the crowd as a heavy cavalry would do while not as heavily armed.
entities.name: Lanzas de Castilla

desc: The Almogavars, embracing new innovations, have undergone remarkable adaptations to enhance their efficiency on the battlefield. Integrating cutting-edge weaponry and strategic advancements into their traditional tactics, these formidable warriors have become even more formidable. With a blend of ancient expertise and modern tools, they stand as a prime example of the seamless fusion between tradition and innovation in warfare.
entities.name: Reformed Almogavars

desc: The Late Cavaliers are the last vestiges of mounted nobility on the battlefield, clad in half-armor and wielding pistols and sabers.
entities.name: Late Cavaliers

desc: Adapting to the changing warfare, the Crusader Sergeants have adopted new tactics and refined weaponry. With these adaptions they will retain their status as the elite foot forces of the Military Orders, side by side with the Order Knights.
entities.name: Order Sergeants

desc: Adapting to the changing warfare, the Crusader Sergeants have adopted new tactics and refined weaponry. With these adaptions they will retain their status as the elite foot forces of the Military Orders, side by side with the Order Knights.
entities.name: Order Sergeants

desc: Adapting to the changing warfare, the Crusader Sergeants have adopted new tactics and refined weaponry. With these adaptions they will retain their status as the elite foot forces of the Military Orders, side by side with the Order Knights.
entities.name: Order Sergeants

desc: A blend of old and new, these Late Gallowglass are heavily-armored troops outfitted with a medley of modern weapons such as arquebus guns to complement their traditional greatswords and axes.
entities.name: Late Gallowglass

desc: Armed with rudimentary armor and their trademark blade, these warriors rely on mastering speed, ferocity, and fluent movements. They excel on close combat where the karambit's curved blade is extremely efficient at slashing, hooking, and gutting opponents. The adoption and proliferation of new formations and combat maneuvers has turned these warriors into a fabled armed force, feared throughout the archipelago.
entities.name: Late Karambit Warriors

desc: Small innovations in equipment and organization result in continuous devastating volleys that shatter all but the most heavily armored formations.
entities.name: Reformed Longbowmen

desc: Paiks are foot soldiers of India who are renowned for their offensive and defensive versatility and their skill in archery. As the weapons develop, so does their portfolio of skills. Thus, the bows of the early eras have been replaced by the modern musket, yet their versatility still prevails.
entities.name: Late Paik

desc: Paiks are foot soldiers of India who are renowned for their offensive and defensive versatility and their skill in archery. As the weapons develop, so does their portfolio of skills. Thus, the bows of the early eras have been replaced by the modern musket, yet their versatility still prevails.
entities.name: Late Paik Infantry

desc: Dressed in characteristic wings and donning illustrious armor, these cavalrymen are a force to be reckoned with when it comes to their powerful charges, dealing immense damage and shattering the enemy's morale.
entities.name: Late Winged Hussars

desc: The Early Legionaries uphold the oldest traditions of drill and discipline. Spears, broad shields, and firm cohesion let them stand fast even as the battle twists around them.
entities.name: Early Legionaries

desc: Legionaries trained in the refined arts of close combat, carrying throwing spears and short swords. Their strength lies in steady formations and a military culture of relentless practice.
entities.name: Legionaries

desc: The Reformed Legionaries are hardened infantrymen, equipped with the best armor and weapons, who form the core of our armies.
entities.name: Reformed Legionaries

desc: The Heavy Legionaries are elite infantrymen, equipped with the finest armor and weapons. Like the heavy armored legions of ancient Rome, these troops will be the hammer with which we will smite our enemies.
entities.name: Heavy Legionaries

desc: The Guard Legionaries embody the highest standard of soldiering within the legions. Selected from the finest cohorts, they are trusted with critical missions and the protection of the state's highest institutions.
entities.name: Guard Legionaries

desc: These Imperial Legionaries stand at the apex of centuries of military evolution. Masters of equipment and doctrine alike, they serve the lifeguard whose presence alone can steady wavering lines.
entities.name: Imperial Legionaries

desc: (This is just a template, should never be seen)
entities.name: Light Cavalry

desc: Light Dragoons are a type of light cavalry that can move, dismount, and shoot at the enemy with the rifles they carry, but are also armed with cavalry sabers, which allow them to charge the enemy if the opportunity arises.
entities.name: Light Dragoons

desc: (This is just a template, should never be seen)
entities.name: Light Infantry

desc: A light complement to our heavy cavalry, their role is to pursue routed enemies and cut them down.
entities.name: Light Jurchen Cavalry

desc: Light Lancers are a type of light cavalry more focused on shock combat, as they use a charging lance, also wearing some degree of armor. However, they base their success on the battlefield on maintaining a high degree of mobility.
entities.name: Light Lancers

gate: is capital in south america or carribean

desc: Lodge Warriors are the most proven fighters of our people, bound by sacred oaths sworn within the Warrior Lodge. Heavily armed and resolute, they anchor the line of battle and inspire those who fight beside them.
entities.name: Lodge Warriors

desc: A strict operation consisting of supply trains and an efficient bureaucracy, Logistics Corps represent the pinnacle of military organization during the Revolutions to support vast armies.
entities.name: Logistics Corps

desc: The Longbowmen excel not only due to their powerful warbow but also their years of training on the archery fields.
entities.name: Longbowmen

desc: The so-called \"galoys ove lour lances\" are light infantry famed for their agile use of heavy spears. Once the scrummage inevitably collapses, they brandish great knives to finish off more heavily-armored foes.
entities.name: Lour Lances

desc: Adorned with brightly-colored regalia and fluttering pennants, Mailed Knights are a sight to behold in any army. But it is their shimmering mail and sharpened steel, along with a lifetime of training, that makes them amongst the hardiest warriors on the battlefield.
entities.name: Mailed Knights

desc: Like their foot brethren, the mounted Mamālīk undergo renewed training and discipline reforms. The mounted core of our standing army remains the elite shock cavalry of the sultanate.
entities.name: Reformed Mamālīk Horsemen

desc: The mounted arm of the Mamlūk military, these elite slave-soldier cavalry form the iconic shock force of our armies. Trained from youth in horsemanship, archery, and the lance, they complement the foot-based Early Mamālīk regiments and project the power of the sultanate across the battlefield.
entities.name: Mamālīk Horsemen

desc: The later Mamlūk troops are categorized by a renewed attention to detail and discipline. A series of military reforms are set in place, to restore the old standards and retrain our standing armies.
entities.name: Reformed Mamālīk

desc: Well-trained elite troops, these men have been honed to represent the best our people have to offer. Raised as slaves purchased from foreign masters, they are disciplined and taught our religious and military doctrines as they are expected to form the core of our standing army. Oftentimes, they come equipped with heavy armor and sturdy spears. Their unique helmets and presence in the battlefield is a terrifying sight for our foes.
entities.name: Early Mamālīk

desc:
The Mandekalu Horsemen are the additional support of the Malian military. These Horon - the free people of Mali - received their mount and equipment from the Ton-tigi and the Mansa. Charging into the battle with lances and long swords, the Mandekalu Horsemen projected the power of the Mansa even in the furthest corners of the empire.

''Can gain Experience in order to be promoted to Farari Infantry and Farari Cavalry after the advance Farari Corps has been researched. Experience is shared by all Mandekalu units. Won battles grant {{green|+15}}, lost battles grant {{green|+5}} Experience per participating Mandekalu unit.''
entities.name: Mandekalu Horsemen

desc:
The Mandekalu Infantry are the backbone of the Malian military, and are made of the Horon - the free people of Mali. Equipped with javelins, bows and poisoned arrows, they are a formidable force to be reckoned with.

''Can gain Experience in order to be promoted to Farari Infantry and Farari Cavalry after the advance Farari Corps has been researched. Experience is shared by all Mandekalu units. Won battles grant {{green|+15}}, lost battles grant {{green|+5}} Experience per participating Mandekalu unit.''
entities.name: Mandekalu Infantry

desc: The development of the matchlock arquebus makes it possible to arm large numbers of soldiers with gunpowder weapons on a scale that was not possible in the Middle Ages.
entities.name: Matchlock Levy

desc: The Mauricians are a very mobile infantry unit that shots its volleys by lines of shooters, so that while a line recharges their arms, the next is firing at the enemy. This rotation gives them a tremendous power over their enemies.
entities.name: Mauricians

desc: Armored footmen outfitted with a medley of hand-to-hand weapons, Men-at-Arms are heavy melee infantry who can break through enemy formations.
entities.name: Men-at-Arms

desc: The generalization of muskets as the main firearms during the 17th century allows local Militiamen units to be deployed as reserve and support units for the main armies on the battlefield.
entities.name: Militiamen

desc: A lifetime of stalking giant moa birds in the rough interior has forged these huntsmen into particularly adept skirmishers.
entities.name: Moa Hunters

desc: The musketeers are the elite fighting force of the royal household. Being a musketeer is a position of great prestige and only nobles with years of military service are allowed to join the company's ranks.
entities.name: Musketeers

desc: Unlike the infantry-based armies of Southern India, these Muslim Riders will allow for much more flexibility in battle.
entities.name: Muslim Riders

desc: Using the secret of the Greek fire, these Naft Throwers throw incendiary grenades at the enemy, using that element in order to not only burn their opponents, but to sow confusion and panic in their ranks. They mainly serve to scare the enemy rather than kill.
entities.name: Naft Throwers

desc: Riding a horse into battle has long been a status symbol amongst the powerful.
entities.name: Noble Cavalry

desc: In a knightly order, its members are required to be proficient in combat, and serve the order's interest in battle. Thus, the Crusader Knights are the best mounted soldiers any order can offer.
entities.name: Crusader Knights

desc: The Order Knights are the most experienced and skilled mounted knights of the order, often leading relatevely small, but skilled units of very heavily armored horsemen into battle under the banner of their Military Order.
entities.name: Order Knights

desc: The elephant is a massive animal with far-reaching tusks and a thick hide. Its ability to traverse any kind of jungle gives the elephant a significant advantage in a very present niche of India. Atop of that, the Orissan War Elephant is capable of withstanding more physical punishment during combat compared to other elephants used for war due to their superior armor and training.
entities.name: Orissan Elephant Cavalry

desc: Paiks are foot soldiers of India who are renowned for their offensive and defensive versatility and their skill in archery.
entities.name: Paik

desc: Paiks are foot soldiers of India who are renowned for their offensive and defensive versatility and their skill in archery.
entities.name: Paik Infantry

desc: Recruited from our Carpathian and Balkan lands, these light troops are well equipped to guard the peace in our border regions. Their knowledge of their homeland will make them a formidable opponent for any invader.
entities.name: Pandur Infantry

desc: A Peasant Levy is formed by commoners summoned for military service by their Lord. The men are meant to bring their own equipment to battle, so the quality of newly created units can vary greatly.
entities.name: Peasant Levy

desc: Pikemen are footmen armed with pikes, allowing them to form dense formations that easily confront enemy cavalry charges, thus negating the power of cavalry on the battlefield.
entities.name: Pikemen

desc: Pistoleers are light cavalrymen armed with pistols, a type of gunpowder weapon that is easier to carry and handle on horseback, but can also be used as a melee weapon, thanks to its heavy, reinforced grip.
entities.name: Pistoleers

desc: Encased in the finest suits of steel armor, these noblemen fight from horseback with maces and hammers designed to crack open helmets and breastplates.
entities.name: Plated Knights

desc: The Swiss Guard is an armed force, formed by unmarried catholic Swiss men, whose mission is to ensure the security of the Pope. Originally hired as a permanent mercenary unit, they became part of the armies of the Holy Father.
entities.name: Swiss Guard

desc: Formed of countryside gentry fulfilling their obligations, the Provincial Cavalry are a competent force of mounted aristocrats.
entities.name: Provincial Cavalry

desc: The Prussian Grenadiers are elite troops of the Prussian Army. Their role as vanguards in sieges and assaults requires them to be fearless fighters, recruited from among the strongest men in our country.
entities.name: Prussian Grenadiers

desc: Developed by a conjunction of imperial gunsmiths and known also as ''Hóngyípào'', this piece of artillery is the epitome of perfection of Asian craftsmanship upon European designs. Based loosely on the Culverin models employed in the West, these cannons have received further improvements, increasing their firepower and reducing their weight.
entities.name: Red Cannon

desc: Redcoats is the name given to the English Line and Column Infantry, after the adoption of red coats by soldiers fighting in Ireland, and their generalization in the New Model Army.
entities.name: Redcoats

desc: The discipline of the Ç̌äwa Regiments gets further improved, making them fight more coordinated, inflicting deadly volleys to their enemies.
entities.name: Ç̌äwa Musketeers

desc: The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.
entities.name: Janissary Musketeers

desc: The Kızılbaş are members of a militant Shia order made of a coalition of different tribes of Turkic-speaking background. Their religious belief plays a major role in their duty, making them both ferocious warriors and devout members of the Ṣafawiyya order.
entities.name: Kızılbaş Cavalry

desc: The gradual influence of continental-style warfare has led to better-equipped and more cohesive units of Gallowglass.
entities.name: Reformed Gallowglass

desc: Some of our countrymen elect to travel into foreign lands and earn their keep as mercenaries for foreign rulers. Once these return to their home, these men are veteran soldiers and some of the best fighters of Europe.
entities.name: Reisläufer

desc: A better structure system allows the Ç̌äwa to be better trained and become a mighty force for Ethiopia.
entities.name: Ç̌äwa Regiments

desc: Under the 'capitulations of conquests', men of the lower nobility or otherwise low status embark to conquer foreign lands for their kings.
entities.name: Early Conquistadors

desc: The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.
entities.name: Janissary Guards

desc: The most modern version of the Ç̌äwa. These fighters have reached the highest point in discipline and effectivity, becoming the terror of their enemies.
entities.name: Ç̌äwa Columns

desc: The Janissaries are the elite corps only loyal to the Sultan himself. Their ranks are made up through the Devşirme System of child levy and go through strict military training. As such, the Janissaries are the most disciplined forces of the Empire.
entities.name: Janissary Columns

desc: From the second half of the 17th century the use of artillery on the battlefield became more widespread. The troops were now able to move their field guns with much more ease and speed.
entities.name: Royal Mortar

desc: The ''Defensioner'' are veteran troops from the rough lands on the Bohemian border. Tasked with securing the passes in the Ore Mountains, these units will serve us well in battles on rough terrain.
entities.name: Saxon Defensioner

desc: A bristling wall of pikes and shields, a Schiltron can hold fast against charges at the cost of mobility.
entities.name: Schiltron

desc: The noble clans of the Highlands are an invaluable asset to our military. With their old formations adapted to the age of muskets, which became famous as the '''Highland Charge''', these clansmen will charge at the enemy and deliver a devastating blow to the enemies' morale with their broadswords.
entities.name: Scottish Highlander

desc: The Hussars are a light cavalry unit whose origin can be traced back to bands of mounted Serb warriors. Their light armor and fast horses allow them to outmaneuver any other regiment, opening the door to the development of innovative strategies.
entities.name: Serbian Hussars

desc: Sharpshooters are a type of light infantry unit made up of the best marksmen, who use rifles with a longer range, making them better at skirmishing and disrupting enemy formations while maneuvering.
entities.name: Sharpshooters

desc: Even when other countries have already discarded the use of elephants in war, the Siamese have continued using them, adapting them to the new conditions modern war supposes.
entities.name: Siamese Elephant Cavalry

desc: Slaves who were trained in the arts of war so they can serve the state as soldiers. Although they receive their weapons from the Horon (the free men of Mali), it is them who risk their lives in combat.
entities.name: Sofa Infantrymen

desc: The Sowar Cavalry is the heavy cavalry of the Mughals. They are notorious for their enduring discipline and their terrifying shock charge which eliminates any semblance of hope for the enemy.
entities.name: Sowar Cavalry

desc: Mongol children are taught how to ride a horse and shoot a bow, and are expected to join the raiding bands when they grow up. In a Horde, men combine peasant activities during peacetime, usually consisting in pastoralism, and military duties whenever the leader of the tribe requires it.
entities.name: Steppe Horde Militia

desc: Riders from the Steppes have specialized in two ways of mounted combat: lances or archery. For the latter, the development of stronger but smaller bows has given them the mobility of the horses and the accuracy and fast volley that short bows provide, making them ideal for hit-and-run tactics.
entities.name: Horse Archers

desc: The Supply Carts are the lifeline of any army wanting to venture outside home territories. They provided food to the men and the animals, extending the distance the army could travel before stopping to forage what can be very hostile lands.
entities.name: Supply Carts

desc: The transition from feudal levies to standing armies in the Discovery is allowing longer campaigns, creating the need to supply those soldiers for longer periods. That comes from the more organized Supply Convoy.
entities.name: Supply Convoy

desc: The Tercio is an elite military unit inside the Spanish Armies, famed for its battlefield formations. Considered some of the finest warriors in Western Europe, the Tercios are one of the region's first modern professional armies.
entities.name: Tercio

desc: A marriage of the Celtic and Continental martial traditions, the Teulu are mounted knights who nimbly dominate rough terrain.
entities.name: Teulu

desc: War elephants have been used in Indochina for generations, both for cavalry and as personal mounts for the kings, who would then engage in elephant duels with the opposing side's leader.
entities.name: Thai Elephant Cavalry

desc: Serving as a standing mercenary army for the Kingdom of Hungary, Hungarian Black Army is a full-time war-focused army, in contrast to other mercenary armies across Europe. They use an unusually high ratio of fire weapons for the period.
entities.name: Hungarian Black Army

desc: The Tofangchi are the musketeers of the empire. Although firearms have been in use before already, their presence has been highly irregular as many of the Persian military prefer to use their traditional weapon of bow and arrow. The regiments of the Tofangchi aim to change this as they are trained in the usage of the modern weaponry.
entities.name: Tofangchi

desc:
Many of the tribes living on the outskirts of our country base their existence around the raising and caring of horses and cattle, by living their whole lives around these animals, they are bound to raise great riders among their midst.

On the rare occasion when a strong hand manages to organize this unruly fighters into a semi coherent unit they form a fast and surprisingly effective force.
entities.name: Tribal Cavalry

desc: Brandishing a variety of implements and simple weapons, Tribesmen are agrarian villagers raised to protect their homes and their kin.
entities.name: Tribesmen

desc: The Tupchi - ''artillery-men'' - are a specialized military unit that focuses on the usage of cannons and siege weapons. Similar to the Tofangchi, the Tupchi are an example of modern warfare exercised by the Persian Empire.
entities.name: Tupchi

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Varangian Guard

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Restored Varangians

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Pelekyphóroi Varangians

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Modernized Varangians

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Imperial Varangians

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Imperial Varangian Guard

desc: This unit, formed by armed peasants without military training, is no more than a desperate attempt to face enemies, a last line of defense against an invader force.
entities.name: Villagers

desc: During the Hussite Wars, our armies relied on wagon forts called ''Wagenburg'' to win battles against superior forces. While we may not always deploy wagons, the principle remains: infantry sharpshooters fighting from prepared defensive positions become our standard doctrine.
entities.name: Wagenburg

desc: The growth in the size of armies during the Absolutism is making their logistics increasingly complex, making each army dependent on its own Wagon Train to maintain its combat performance in the field.
entities.name: Wagon Train

gate: is capital in south america or carribean

desc: A War Party is a swift raiding force drawn from warrior society traditions across North America. Trained from childhood in hunting and warfare, they carry bows, war clubs, and tomahawks, excelling at ambushes and hit-and-run raids.
entities.name: War Party

desc: Warriors are the name given to tribal fighters following the command of their leaders. Their weaponry can vary depending on their origins, but can be considered somewhat simple, yet effective.
entities.name: Warriors

desc: Dressed in characteristic wings and donning illustrious armor, these cavalrymen are a force to be reckoned with when it comes to their powerful charges, dealing immense damage and shattering the enemy's morale.
entities.name: Winged Hussars

desc: The Baltic Sea can be a dangerous place to navigate with warships. Its treacherous shallow waters require ships to operate with a small draft, otherwise risking loss of navigation and effectiveness. The Archipelago Frigate, a sailing ships equipped with oars, is well suited for the waters of the Baltic and will grant an edge in swiftness and lethality to the navy.
entities.name: Archipelago Frigate

desc: Serving as larger variants of the Sekibune ships, the Atakebune is able to staff a larger crew than before. Sometimes equipped with iron or copper plates mounted on the hull, they improve on the survivability of the previous types as well.
entities.name: Atakebune

desc: The Baghlah is a large deep-sea sailing vessel which is used as a merchant ship. It has its origins in the Arabian Peninsula, but spread as far as the Spice Islands as a used ship type.
entities.name: Baghlah

desc: The Bǎochuán is a large vessel designed to transport goods and protect the trade on sea. They are capable of long distance voyages, bringing treasure and tribute from far away shores to our lands.
entities.name: Bǎochuán

desc: The Barque was a small sailing ship, originally used for trade. Adapting these for warfare provided a smaller and faster alternative to the larger carracks.
entities.name: Barque

desc: The light galleys belonging to local chieftains connect our islands together, but can be levied in times of war.
entities.name: Birlinn

desc: The Bomb Ketch is a specialized light ship to carry out shore bombardments. Sacrificing most of their cannons in exchange for mortars able to carry out heavy bombardment of stationary targets along the shoreline, these vessels can trivialize the siege of coastal fortifications.
entities.name: Bomb Ketch

desc: The brig was a small ship used for trade or war, characterized by having two square-rigged masts. When used for war, they were small vessels with 10 to 18 guns, but it was their speed and maneuverability what made them valuable assets. Their full square rigging also made them more suited when traveling along trade winds, when they would sail downwind for long periods of time.
entities.name: Brig

desc: A large and heavily armed ship, propelled by oars and two or even three sails, the Cakradonya will dominate the seas of Indonesia.
entities.name: Cakradonya

desc: Small boats propelled with paddles, canoes are primitive vessels for ferrying small numbers of warriors over waterways.
entities.name: Canoe

desc: The caravel was a small, very maneuverable ship which could sail with high precision on long discovery journeys. Although designs varied, a caravel had a foresail, a square mainsail and a lateen mizzen. Its smaller size limited the number of guns onboard, but it also meant that this light ship could explore shallow coastal waters and estuaries. Vasco Da Gama, Cabot, Columbus and Magellan used caravels during their late 15th century and early 16th century voyages.
entities.name: Caravel

desc: The design of the carrack, a late medieval ship, combined the features of Germanic longships and Arabic merchantmen. It was less maneuverable than the caravel, but because of its larger size, it could carry provisions for long voyages, cargo for trade, and guns for self-defense. Some carracks such as the English vessel 'Henri Grâce à Dieu' weighed more than 1,000 tons, had large fore and aft castles, and could be considered as the greatest warships of their time.
entities.name: Carrack

desc: An original invention from the Iberian Mediterranean coasts, the Catalan Galley dominated the western Mediterranean Sea in fierce competence with the Genoese Galley for supremacy of the waves.
entities.name: Catalan Galley

desc: The cog was a small ship widely used in medieval Europe. Characterized by having a single mast with a square sail, and constructed with overlapping planks, it was an evolution of the Viking merchant ships. Their construction made them more suitable for navigating the North Atlantic than the Mediterranean vessels, while their simpler rigging required fewer people to operate. It was used extensively by the Hanseatic League until eventually replaced by the hulk.
entities.name: Cog

desc: A common trading ship in the Indian Ocean, the Dhow is a capable vessel for trading in the region, despite its small hull size.
entities.name: Dhow

desc: The early carrack was the first European vessel that could sail on the high seas of the Atlantic Ocean. The design of this late medieval ship combined the features of Germanic longships and Arabic merchantmen. It was less maneuverable than the caravel, but because of its larger size, it could carry provisions for long voyages, cargo for trade, and guns for self-defense.
entities.name: Early Carrack

desc: The Early Iberian Caravel is a light ship developed in the northwestern coasts of the Iberian Peninsula that would soon spread across the continent.
entities.name: Early Iberian Caravel

desc: The Early Iberian Galleon is a heavy ship developed in the shores of the Iberian Peninsula that every European fleet will adopt.
entities.name: Early Iberian Galleon

desc: The Gwiseon Turtle Ship is a Korean warship which utilizes oars and sails to outmaneuver other types of galleys, while also being equipped with light ''Chongtong'' - Korean firearms.
entities.name: Gwiseon Turtle Ship

desc: The Eastindiaman was a general term for all ships operating for any of the East India Trading Companies. Being able to carry both passengers and goods, they were built at first to carry as much as possible. They were still armed to defend themselves against pirates, so they could also participate in war engagement, but trade was always their main function.
entities.name: East-Indiaman

desc: Small civilian boats, used for collecting fish from the sea, pressed into service as rudimentary troop transport. These are small and defenseless but can be used at a push to move people around, just be careful not to get caught by anyone with cannons.
entities.name: Fishing Boat

desc: A cargo ship developed in the Netherlands in the 16th century, it was built to maximize cargo space and crew efficiency. And it became one of the most commonly used ships in the 16th and 17th centuries. The standard design wasn't armed but when needed it could be armed with cannons and serve as auxiliary vessels.
entities.name: Flute

desc: As time passed, the frigate evolved. It became larger and heavily armed, sometimes with two gun decks. The frigate's combination of speed and firepower meant that it could outrun any ship with more guns and outgun any faster ships. The fleet built by the Commonwealth of England in the 1650s consisted almost exclusively of frigates.
entities.name: Frigate

desc: A fast variant of a galley, the Galiot is well suited for the waters of the Mediterranean Sea, being able to navigate both shallow and deep sea.
entities.name: Galiot

desc: The galleass was an adaptation of the large merchant galley to counter the increasing use of man-of-war. Larger than the galley, the galleass had about 32 oar pairs, each oar manned by up to five men. As an answer to the men-of-war's armament and higher sides, the galleass had forecastles and aftcastles and gun decks above the rowers. This extra weight meant that they also had to rely more on sails, and were slower and less maneuverable compared to galleys. Like the galley, the galleass went out of regular use with the introduction of more advanced oceangoing men-of-war, but remained useful in shallow waters until the 18th century.
entities.name: Galleass

desc: A large, usually three-masted sailing ship originally designed as a warship but later on used primarily for trade and commerce.
entities.name: Galleon

desc: The Genoese Galley is the backbone of the Genoese navy. Lighter and longer than other galleys used in the Mediterranean Sea, this ship is able to achieve unmatched speed while also having a significant cargo advantage at the cost of maneuverability and durability.
entities.name: Genoese Galley

desc: The adapting of the Greek Fire deployment system to the newer types of ships allows it to continue reducing our enemy's boats to ashes, and it remains as a symbol of our navy as a whole.
entities.name: Advanced Siphōnes

desc: Equipped with the special tubes to deploy the Greek fire, these vessels unfold an inferno of flames onto the enemy ships, turning them to cinder in no time. At close range, they herald only but destruction.
entities.name: Siphōnes

desc: The Hanseatic Cog is the pride of our trade fleet. Originally conceived during the late 12th century, it has been redesigned and improved continuously over the next hundred years. Characterized by its bulbous shape, single mast, square sail, stern rudder, and flat bottom, it revolutionized cargo transportation. Its design facilitated navigation in shallow waters, making it highly practical for trade. With a modest crew, a cog could efficiently transport substantial cargo, providing the Hanseatic League with a distinct edge in commerce over its rivals.
entities.name: Hanseatic Cog

desc: The heavy frigate was introduced by the British in the 18th century as a larger variant of the frigate in terms of both size and power of its guns. Having more and bigger guns meant an increase in their firepower and resulted in ships of individually greater force. Heavy frigates became the standard frigates during the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars.
entities.name: Heavy Frigate

desc: The hulk was a type of European ship, the predecessor of the carrack and caravel, that originated in the Low Countries as a river boat, and was used predominantly as a cargo vessel, although it could be also used in war. It was constructed with a single mast with a square sail, and with a castle on both ends of the ship. Capable of rivaling the cog's carrying capacity, the hulk was the main trade ship used by the Hanseatic League.
entities.name: Hulk

desc: The Early Iberian Caravel becomes obsolete with the Iberian Caravel that evolves to surpass the already widespread Caravel with a better design in the sails and better armament. These ships will be the spearhead of the Age of Discovery.
entities.name: Iberian Caravel

desc: The Iberian Galleon is the evolution of the Early Iberian Galleon that will show the power of the Iberian naval techniques to the rest of the world.
entities.name: Iberian Galleon

desc: The galleass was an adaptation of the large merchant galley to counter the increasing use of man-of-war. Larger than the galley, the galleass had about 32 oar pairs, each oar manned by up to five men. As an answer to the men-of-war's armament and higher sides, the galleass had forecastles and aftcastles and gun decks above the rowers. This extra weight meant that they also had to rely more on sails, and were slower and less maneuverable compared to galleys. Like the galley, the galleass went out of regular use with the introduction of more advanced oceangoing men-of-war, but remained useful in shallow waters until the 18th century.
entities.name: Italian Galleass

desc: The Jong has proudly served our people for a long time. Its characteristic number of masts and hull are made of thick wood, making it the perfect vessel for a combination of ferrying goods across long distances, as well as troops.
entities.name: Jong

desc: Used widely across the entirety of the Indonesia, the Kabang is a versatile ship of medium size and often crafted from a single piece of wood. Beyond its role as transport of people and goods, it has come to be synonymous with sea nomads. These folk consist of populations of peasants and fishermen who used the tide and monsoons to migrate from port to port, making a living off the sea.
entities.name: Kabang

desc: Known for their slender and elongated hull design, the Kilwan Dhow is famous for being the backbone of our maritime trade that connects our ports to faraway lands. The ship itself is a manifestation of our mastery of shipwright, as our workers utilize palm trees for a sturdy body as well as locally-grown cotton for the sails.
entities.name: Kilwan Dhow

desc: The Kilwan Zambuc is a smaller variation of the Kilwan Dhow, and it is primarily used for local trade, transportation of goods and pottery between the various city-states across the Swahili Coast, as well as serving as trustworthy faring vessels for short distances.
entities.name: Kilwan Zambuc

desc: The ships of Ireland and the Highlands are most capable at projecting our presence over our coastal possessions, protecting merchant vessels and at the same time, serving as adequate warships in times of need.
entities.name: Long Fada

desc: An improved Long Fada, the Great Long Fada is a larger vessel with more oars and a bigger crew, able to carry out longer voyages and project more power over the seas.
entities.name: Great Long Fada

desc: The people that populate the Madura Strait have come to serve in our navy. Their naval prowess and great shipbuilding skills have given rise to a new kind of vessel, the Madurese Ghali. A large ship, it is used for offensive and voyager-adjacent tasks, as it will soon comprise the backbone of our fleet.
entities.name: Madurese Ghali

desc: With roots back to the ancient ships of antiquity, the galley remained the prime choice for Mediterranean naval warfare until the 16th century. The galley was primarily propelled by oars, usually about 25 pairs manned by up to three men each. This meant that they were less dependent on wind gauges compared to sailing ships, and their maneuverability made them a feared adversary. Eventually, the galley went out of regular use with the introduction of more advanced oceangoing men-of-war, but remained useful in shallow waters until the 18th century.
entities.name: Mediterranean Galley

desc: Merchantman is a type of ship used for commerce carrying goods or passengers. They would generally include some armament to protect themselves from pirates and privateers, especially if engaging in long travels, in which case they could even be heavily armed.
entities.name: Merchantman

desc: One of the most common ship types and a predecessor to the standard Kilwan Dhow, the Mtepe is connected to Swahili as a steadfast cornerstone of their maritime prowess. Unlike the Kilwan Dhow, the Mtepe has a square stern and its core construction does not use nails. Instead, a sewn-plank construction is utilized, bonding the hull together. The primary role of the Mtepe is to navigate the shallow local waters and establish maritime trade across the coast of Africa.
entities.name: Mtepe

desc: The Panokseon is a multi-deck warship with greater size and firepower than the usual Geobukseon Turtle Ship. While still relying on oars, the sails of the Panokseon allow it to reach a greater speed comparable to galleys for its size.
entities.name: Panokseon

desc: With the increasing overseas trade, there was a need for a fast escort vessel to provide a safe journey. The Pinnace was developed for this. It was a smaller, leaner warship with one gun deck, and it provided protection from piracy in dangerous waters.
entities.name: Pinnace

desc: Build from cider or fir wood, the Sekibune sacrifices a sturdy hull for increased speed and maneuverability.
entities.name: Sekibune

desc: Some alterations to the standard Three-decker design, these ships will serve as flagships and the pride of the navy. While they are expensive to operate, these ships are potentially able to win combats on their own, due to their sturdier hull and superior firepower.
entities.name: First-Rate Ship of the Line

desc: The Square-Rigged Caravel is a Portuguese invention that is born from the combination of the Iberian Caravel and the Carrack. This ship combines the swiftness of the former and the structure and durability of the latter, making it an ideal ship for fight and exploration.
entities.name: Square-Rigged Caravel

desc: Three-deckers were warships that held three fully-armed decks with guns. Other guns could also be carried additionally on the forecastle or the quarterdeck, but only the batteries of the three main decks formed a continuous battery. Three-deckers were considered ships of the line, that is strong enough to participate in the line of battle.
entities.name: Three-decker

desc: Galleys of various forms have dominated the seas for millennia, and many remote shipwrights still construct them in the traditional ways. The skill of ship construction is passed down from generation to generation, although with little innovation.
entities.name: Traditional Galley

desc: The evolution of the Gwiseon Turtle Ship, the advanced Geobukseon Turtle Ship model has an increased bulwark height to increase its durability without hindering its mobility.
entities.name: Geobukseon Turtle Ship

desc: Two-deckers were warships that held two fully-armed decks with guns. Other guns could also be carried additionally on the forecastle or the quarterdeck, but only the batteries of the two main decks formed a continuous battery.
entities.name: Two-decker

desc: Refocusing the design of the Galleon towards duties of warfare, the War Galleon will give us a great advantage in naval warfare.
entities.name: War Galleon

desc: War galleys are galleys used for war. They are long and shallow, propelled mainly by oars, although they generally also included some kind of sail. Used since ancient times, their presence was commonplace in the seas and oceans during the Middle Ages thanks to their higher maneuverability. Being used for boarding rather than long-range engagements, projectile weapons and guns were concentrated on the front of the ship, leaving the protection of the weak spots of the sides and the rear to the ability to out-maneuver their enemies.
entities.name: War Galley

desc: A two or three-masted small vessel widely used in the Mediterranean from the 16th century onwards.
entities.name: Xebec
